_doc: The combined likelihood. Read by mf/trexcfg.adapt_channel; every entry is explained in README.md. tautau is the four-channel measurement of z-tautau (tau_h tau_h + mu tau_h + e tau_h + e mu, commits b7ec3d9 inputs / e0b0b1d results, z-tautau/docs/11-combination-inputs.md); the frozen three-channel combination is at the git tag zmumu-freeze-2026-09-17.
observable: sigma(pp -> Z/gamma* -> ll), 60 < m_ll(LHE) < 120 GeV, sqrt(s) = 13 TeV, per lepton flavour, lepton universality

poi.name: mu_Z
poi.title: #mu_{Z}
poi.reference_note: aMC@NLO (NNLO-normalised) sigma(60 < m_LHE(mumu) < 120) of z-mumu; sigma = mu_Z x reference_pb

ee.label: ee
ee.sigma_reference_source: z-ee/Zee_fit.tar.gz: Zee_fit/reference_cross_section.txt (6077.22 pb x sum w(LHE ee, 60-120) / sum w)
ee.acceptance_note: none outside the fit: the DYee template is normalised to the 60-120 GeV LHE cross section and its PDF / QCDScale / PS_FSR templates carry the extrapolation
ee.split_shape_norm_note: every HISTO systematic of ee enters twice: its normalisation keeps the shared name (correlated with mumu/tautau), its shape gets an ee-only parameter <NP>_eeShape. Without it the ee peak shape (6.3M events in 2 GeV bins, saturated-model p = 7e-43) pins the +-5.9% ElectronID normalisation at 0.08 sigma and drags Pileup/L1Prefiring/QCDScale into mumu; the fully correlated three-channel fit then has no positive-definite minimum. See README.md, 'The ee channel'.

mumu.label: #mu#mu
mumu.drop_regions_note: mumu_CRemu (exactly one muon and one electron, opposite sign) selects the same data as the tautau e-mu channel (emu_SR, emu_CRtt). It is Type VALIDATION in z-mumu/fit/zmumu.config, so it never entered the mumu likelihood and dropping it cannot change a fit; it is removed so that no combination workspace, table or plot holds those events twice. With it go the WJets sample and the XS_WJets / ElectronEff_mumu parameters of mumu, which act only there. checks.mumu_cremu_control measures what the region would do as a control region of mumu.

acceptance.note: 60-120 GeV denominator (z-mumu/zmumu/acceptance.py, frozen 17 Sep 2026). Until the freeze Acc_PDF, Acc_AlphaS, Acc_QCDScale and Acc_PS_FSR were shared with the tau_h tau_h-only tautau (v3), which quoted sigma_fid / A as well; tautau v4 carries its acceptance inside its PDF / QCDScale / PS_* templates, so these parameters are now mumu-only. They are deliberately not merged into PDF / QCDScale / PS_FSR: the four tautau final states constrain QCDScale through their acceptance ratios (z-tautau/docs/11 section 5) and that constraint must not shrink the mumu acceptance uncertainty. Acc_PTZ_mumu is the pT(Z) spectrum reweighted to the measured pT(mumu) (larger than the PYTHIA ISR weights, which it replaces), Acc_Generator_mumu powheg vs aMC@NLO, Acc_QEDFSR_mumu the QED FSR estimate (option c of z-mumu/docs/16): all three are sized or derived in the mumu channel only, hence channel-suffixed. Until 16 Sep the block had PDF, alpha_s, scale and statistics for the m > 50 GeV denominator (0.61 %); now 0.70 %.

tautau.label: #tau#tau
tautau.label_note: four final states in one likelihood: tau_h tau_h (3 BDT categories), mu tau_h and e tau_h (4 decay-mode regions each), e mu (signal region + ttbar control region); the 13 regions of z-tautau/fit/ztautau.config, never the pT-split copies
tautau.signal_note: mu_Z acts on the 15 DYtautau_tDM* templates (Z/gamma* -> tautau, 60 < m_LHE < 120 GeV, all decays, split by the decay mode of the genuine tau_h legs); DYtautau_out is a background
tautau.rename_systematics_note: decorrelated from mumu and ee: tautau takes its muon ID / isolation / trigger / scale and electron ID / reco / scale from the POG jsons, z-mumu measures its own with tag-and-probe and z-ee's ElectronID is the +-5.9 % gap artefact. Same names would claim they are one measurement (TRExFitter correlates by name). variations.tautau_leptons_correlated is the fit with that claim.
tautau.acceptance_note: none outside the fit: the theory templates are renormalised to a constant sigma(60-120), so PDF / QCDScale / PS_ISR / PS_FSR vary A x epsilon inside the likelihood (z-tautau/docs/11-combination-inputs.md section 3, metadata acceptance_in_fit). Until the freeze (tau_h tau_h only) this was a 3.7 % block of Acc_* parameters.
tautau.drop_empty_bins_note: none: tautau_SR2 bin 1 (0 data, 0 prediction) is dropped by z-tautau's own config since b7ec3d9 (DropBins). Re-derived on the v4 inputs: it is the only bin of the 13 regions with no prediction; tautau_SR1 bin 1 and tautau_SR2 bin 13 have 0 data but 0.8 and 2.0 predicted events, which is an ordinary Poisson term.
tautau.ttbar_note: tautau normalises ttbar with a free mu_ttbar (from emu_CRtt) and has no XS_TTbar; mumu and ee constrain it with XS_TTbar (6 %). All three use the same powheg samples and 831.76 pb. Baseline: two parameters, each in its own channel -- mu_ttbar = 1.10 absorbs what is specific to the e-mu control region (its trigger efficiency, MET > 80 GeV and D_zeta modelling), which the CMS ttbar cross section (data/theory ~ 1.0) says is not sigma(ttbar). variations.ttbar_cr_for_all_channels shares the control-region factor with mumu and ee (no XS_TTbar prior there); variations.ttbar_xs_constrained has one 6 % XS_TTbar everywhere and no free factor, so that emu_CRtt constrains it for every channel.
tautau.modelling_note: z-tautau/docs/11-combination-inputs.md section 7.3: the tautau fit assumes one tau_h ID scale factor per decay mode for every pT. Their cross-check with separate scale factors below 40 GeV in the l tau_h regions moves mu_Z from 1.019 to 0.954 (-6.3 %, 1.8x their total uncertainty), which no parameter of their fit covers; they ask a combination that wants a conservative tautau input to carry it. It enters as one OVERALL parameter on the tautau signal, its size read from their two published fits. variations.tautau_as_delivered is the fit without it, variations.tautau_ptsplit the fit with their pT-split model instead.

published_submeasurements._doc: z-tautau's own fits of parts of its data, shown next to the combination's tautau line (figure tautau_channels); mu x sigma_reference_pb

fit._doc: extra Fit/MultiFit options for every likelihood. FitStrategy 3 (Minuit2 'very high': central finite differences for the Hessian and NO forcing of a non-positive-definite matrix). With strategy 2 MINUIT returns status 0 everywhere but HESSE runs on a matrix 'forced pos-def by adding to diagonal': HESSE error on mu_Z 8x below MINOS (0.0018 vs 0.0152), Lumi post-fit error 0.15, mu_Z most correlated with a single tautau MC-statistics gamma -- the covariance, and with it the uncertainty groups, the post-fit NP errors and the +-1 sigma points of the ranking, is useless, while MINOS on mu_Z is right. The frozen three-channel fit asked for strategy 2 too, but there MIGRAD failed at 2 and TRExFitter escalated to 3 by itself, which is why its covariance was good (work_freeze_2026-09-17/common/logs/multifit_mwf.log); the four-channel tautau likelihood 'converges' at 2, so nothing escalates. With 3: HESSE/MINOS = 1.001, Lumi 0.97, same minimum, 66 s. NLLOffset 'bin' would help the precision of the 2M-event bins but ROOT 6.40 returns NaN for bins with zero observed events (RooFit::Detail::MathFuncs::nll, 0 x log 0), which tautau has (tautau_SR1 bin 1, tautau_SR2 bin 13). NumCPU 4: what the HTCondor slots of mf/condor.py request. MaximumNumberFCNcalls 2000000: the central-difference HESSE of strategy 3 needs about twice the calls; with TRExFitter's default (500 per parameter) the ee + mumu likelihood ends with 'MnHesse maximum number of function calls exhausted', status 300 and a segfault.

ranking_fit._doc: overrides of 'fit' for the ranking refits (run.py impacts, multifit_ranking.config). FitStrategy -1 is TRExFitter's default: start at strategy 1 and retry at 2 and 3 if a fit fails. With an explicit strategy 2 only one retry is left, and 27 of the 75 refits failed (MINUIT status 3, recorded as a POI of 0); with the default all converge. The nominal fit they start from, and the post-fit errors that set the +-1 sigma points, stay strategy 2.

variations._doc: Alternative likelihoods, each fitted with the common POI only (run.py variations). 'channels' restricts the fit; 'split' overrides split_shape_norm per channel; 'overall' replaces the normalisation part of a split systematic by a symmetric OVERALL of that size; 'fit' overrides entries of the top-level 'fit' options for this likelihood. 'channel_overrides' replaces entries of a channel's specification.

fit._doc: strategy 3 ends in an invalid minimum here (MIGRAD status 3; with ~50 extra tautau shape parameters and the TauIDpT_tautau normalisation). Strategy 2 and strategy 1 both converge with status 0 and agree on the MINOS interval of mu_Z (1.0028 +0.0161 -0.0159), which is the only thing used from a variation; their HESSE matrix is forced positive-definite (pos_def_forced is recorded in result.json).

ee_electron_id_1p2.label: ee: ElectronID norm. #pm1.2%
ee_electron_id_1p2.note: diagnostic: the UL2016postVFP Medium-ID SF map (datasets/corrections, POG/EGM) gives +-0.3-1.6% per electron outside the ECAL gap, 1.2% per Z->ee event; inside 1.444 < |eta_SC| < 1.566, which z-ee does not veto, it is sf = 1 +- 1. Not a result: it uses a number z-ee did not deliver.

tautau_as_delivered.label: #tau#tau as delivered (no #tau_{h} ID p_{T} uncertainty)
tautau_as_delivered.note: the tautau likelihood exactly as z-tautau publishes it (1981 +73 -70 pb alone)

tautau_ptsplit.label: #tau#tau: p_{T}-split #tau_{h} ID SF model
tautau_ptsplit.note: z-tautau's cross-check model (l tau_h regions split at pT(tau_h) = 40 GeV, own scale factors below) in place of the nominal one: the effect TauIDpT_tautau stands for, fitted instead of assigned

tautau_emu_only.label: #tau#tau: e#mu channel only
tautau_emu_only.note: the sub-measurement without any tau_h (z-tautau: 0.960 +0.042 -0.040); docs/11 section 7.1

tautau_tauh_only.label: #tau#tau: #tau_{h} channels only
tautau_tauh_only.note: tau_h tau_h + mu tau_h + e tau_h with free scale factors, no e mu (z-tautau: 1.203 +0.091 -0.084); docs/11 section 7.1

tautau_emutrig2x.label: #tau#tau: e#mu trigger prior #times2
tautau_emutrig2x.note: the pre-review e-mu trigger prior (2 % per leg); docs/11 section 7.2

tautau_leptons_correlated.label: #tau#tau lepton NPs correlated
tautau_leptons_correlated.note: the name-based default the tautau group warned about: MuonID/Iso/Trigger/Scale of tautau (POG) shared with mumu (tag-and-probe), ElectronID/Reco/Scale shared with the normalisation parts of ee's ElectronID/ElectronRECO/ElectronES

tautau_theory_decorrelated.label: #tau#tau theory NPs decorrelated
tautau_theory_decorrelated.note: tautau constrains QCDScale through the acceptance ratios of its four final states; here that constraint cannot reach ee and mumu

ttbar_cr_for_all_channels.label: t#bar{t}: e#mu control region for all channels
ttbar_cr_for_all_channels.note: the free mu_ttbar that emu_CRtt determines also scales ttbar in mumu and ee, instead of their 6 % XS_TTbar prior

ttbar_xs_constrained.label: t#bar{t}: XS_TTbar (6%) everywhere, no free #mu_{t#bar{t}}
ttbar_xs_constrained.note: one 6 % XS_TTbar for all channels, constrained by emu_CRtt, no free factor: the control region then measures Lumi x XS_TTbar x e-mu trigger x b-tag, and its 10 % excess is shared out by prior width -- 0.3 sigma of it to Lumi, which moves every channel

checks._doc: Single-channel likelihoods fitted on their own (run.py: hw + f), compared with the channel's standalone fit of the common likelihood.

mumu_cremu_validation.label: #mu#mu with mumu_CRemu as delivered (validation region)
mumu_cremu_validation.note: must reproduce the standalone mumu fit exactly: a VALIDATION region is not in the likelihood

mumu_cremu_control.label: #mu#mu with mumu_CRemu as a control region
mumu_cremu_control.note: what the e-mu region would add to mumu if it were fitted: the size of what is given up by leaving it to tautau
